title: Common
description: Definitions the stored objects and the envelope share. Not an object of its own.

Sha256.description: A SHA-256 digest as 64 lowercase hex characters.

Timestamp.description: An RFC 3339 time in UTC, as seshi writes it (`2026-11-14T09:00:00.000Z`).

SourceKind.description: How an envelope arrived (X4.1): an upload from the CLI, a capture hook, an OTLP push, or one of the pollers.

SourceId.description: A configured source's id, or `upload` for hooks and the CLI: words of lowercase letters and digits joined by single `-`.

CallerKind.description: Which kind of credential made a call (X5.1, X5.9): `person` (IdP session token or org key with a stated username), `device` (write-only device token), `service` (a service account: a reader, an OTLP destination, a poller), `admin` (an admin token, or the session token of a person with the admin role), `static` (a token from config) or `local` (a serverless laptop writing its owner's folder of the bucket directly, F11.4).

Writer.description: Who wrote something (X5.5): the caller's kind, the person or service account, the credential it used, and the source the data came through.

principal.description: The owner id of the person (X5.8), or `svc:<source-id>` for a service account.

credential_id.description: The id of the token or key used, when it has one; never the secret.

OwnerBasis.description: Why the session belongs to its owner (X5.5): `verified` (an IdP sign-in, or a credential the operator bound to the owner), `claimed` (an org-key caller stated the username, X5.12) or `service` (an org-level source's service account, X5.4).

LogEncoding.description: How a log is encoded: one JSON value per line (`jsonl`), or one JSON document (`json`).

Visibility.description: Who may read a session (X5.10): `org`, every member; `owner`, only its owner. Admins and services see everything.

Labels.description: Small key/value strings attached to a session from config: the CLI's `[labels]`, a repo's `.seshi/config.toml`, a server source's `labels`. seshi gives them no meaning. Keys `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}`, values 1 to 512 characters, at most 32.

Claims.description: Identity the data asserts, copied from a fixed allowlist (X5.5). Never decides ownership (X5.4); with no raw stored, this is the only place it survives.

name.description: A display name the data names.

username.description: A username the caller stated or the data names.

git_email.description: The git `user.email` of the working copy.

git_name.description: The git `user.name` of the working copy.

account_ids.description: Account ids by vendor (`anthropic`, `openai`, `cursor`, …), as the agent records them.

SourceLocation.description: Where in the source the data was read (X4.1): enough to fetch it again for reprocessing (X4.9), never the content.

etag.description: That object's ETag when it was read.

cursor.description: An API cursor or time window, as the poller writes it.

Provenance.description: Which source a write came from and how it was read: the route, the configured source, the format adapter that normalized it and where in the source it was.

format.description: The format adapter the payload was normalized with (`claude-code`, `otlp-genai`, …).

Normalizer.description: Which code normalized the records, so the sessions an adapter fix affects can be picked out and rebuilt (X4.9).

format_version.description: The format adapter's own normalizer version (`1+trajectory.0.3.0`): what the records a transcript normalizes to depend on, compared number by number. On a session's metadata it is the oldest that built any of its stored traces, so a session is stale when it is older than the format's current one (X4.9). Absent on what was written before it was recorded, which counts as stale.

Continuation.description: Marks a trace that is the tail of an already-stored session.

from_record.description: Index of the first record of this trace (after its meta record) within the session's full record list.

prefix_sha256.description: `prefixSha256` of the session's records before it: sha256 of their canonical JSON.

RedactionSummary.description: What redaction did, never what it matched (F2): the rule set that ran, and how many times each rule fired.

rule_set.description: sha256 of the rule set that ran (built-in rules plus the operator's packs).
